value.body: A medical lab technologist collects and processes blood, urine and other samples and runs the tests doctors use for diagnosis. Employers are hospital laboratories, diagnostic chains, blood banks and research labs. A shift involves handling samples, running analysers, doing quality-control checks and recording results for a pathologist to review and sign.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: DMLT is a shorter diploma route

items.label: Regulation
items.value: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Haematology and biochemistry analysers, microscopes, lab information systems

items.label: NABL-accredited medical laboratories
items.note: Accredited labs only; many more unaccredited labs operate
items.source: NABL (Quality Council of India), accredited bodies summary, data as on 30 Sep 2026

items.label: Enrolment, B.M.L.T. (Bachelor in Medical Lab Technology)
items.note: Only the programme named B.M.L.T.; B.Sc MLT and diploma students reported under other names are not included
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 11, all modes, actual responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, then a B.Sc MLT or DMLT with an internship. Freshers usually join hospital or diagnostic labs as lab technicians, often on rotating shifts; government posts are filled through state and central recruitment exams.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles are senior technologist, lab supervisor or quality manager; an M.Sc MLT opens teaching and research.
Night and weekend shifts are common in hospital labs.
NABL-accredited labs expect strict documentation and quality routines.
